items.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: And the first year it was Peter Erskine on drums, the second year it was Dennis Chambers, great drummers and great rhythm sections, great horn sections. I mean Chris Potter was in both editions of that band.

ctx.x: Two different worlds. The music. Steely Dan. Changes, great changes. That was the best gig I ever had I think, of all the gigs. If I had to name one that I loved more than any of the others it was going out with that band that hadn’t gone out in nineteen years, and I’d never been on one of their records. It’s one of the things I’d always wanted to — “I’m going to the Steely Dan date.” “Oh I wish they’d call me.” And then when they finally went out live they called me. And I said all right. This is fun. And the…

anybody. So I said Jeez I’m sorry I can’t do it. And that was the end of my Steely Dan — being an alumnus of Steely Dan. I go back occasionally and sit in, and I love Donald. I don’t get to see Walter that much, but Donald lives up here so I sometimes see him.
